evidenceAudit.scope: Women with bleeding or pain in early pregnancy (under 12–14 weeks) and women with complications after spontaneous or induced abortion in India: threatened, incomplete and missed miscarriage, haemorrhage, shock, and septic abortion. Built on the MoHFW CAC training and service delivery guidelines (2023) and the NCDC-ICMR National Treatment Guidelines (2025) for septic abortion antibiotics, with NICE NG126 for missed and threatened miscarriage regimens the Indian guideline does not cover.
findings: Examination, uterine size interpretation, laboratory tests, vacuum aspiration indications, incomplete abortion (misoprostol 400 micrograms sublingual or 600 micrograms oral, or vacuum aspiration), haemorrhage (misoprostol, uterine massage, oxytocin 10 units in 500 mL), shock resuscitation, post-abortion infection, anti-D 50 micrograms for Rh-negative women and discharge advice checked against MoHFW CAC guidelines 2023, Chapters 4, 6 and 7.

Septic abortion antibiotics (ampicillin, gentamicin and metronidazole; amoxicillin-clavulanate; clindamycin with gentamicin; piperacillin-tazobactam or meropenem with organ dysfunction) checked against NCDC-ICMR National Treatment Guidelines 2025, section 6.3.

Missed miscarriage (mifepristone 200 mg then misoprostol 800 micrograms), threatened miscarriage progesterone, expectant management and anti-D rules checked against NICE NG126 recommendations 1.5 and 1.7.
CAC and NICE differ on when anti-D is needed; shown side by side.
unverifiedSections: The MoHFW CAC guideline does not give a regimen for missed miscarriage or threatened miscarriage; these are from NICE NG126 (off-label use of mifepristone and misoprostol in the UK).
Septic abortion durations (7–10 days) are from NCDC-ICMR NTG; switching to oral therapy is not specified.
Paediatric (adolescent) doses are not separately given; adolescents receive adult obstetric doses in the cited sources.
Gentamicin dosing in kidney impairment and monitoring of levels are not specified in NTG; follow the hospital protocol.
Second-trimester pregnancy loss is outside this topic.
Drug cautions and contraindications without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.
US labels (DailyMed) were used where Indian sources give no dose; confirm against the Indian product label (CDSCO) and hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Miscarriage is loss of a pregnancy before viability; most early losses are due to chromosomal abnormalities. Retained products of conception cause continued bleeding and are the main route to infection. Post-abortion complications — haemorrhage, incomplete evacuation, uterine perforation and sepsis — remain an important cause of maternal death in India. Management depends on the woman's stability, the type of miscarriage and the presence of infection (CAC 2023).
keyMechanisms: Failure of the early pregnancy leads to separation of the gestational sac and bleeding from the placental bed.
Products left in the uterus stop it contracting, causing continued bleeding.
Retained tissue and breaks in asepsis allow ascending infection; sepsis can follow within 24–48 hours (NTG section 6.3).
Uterine instrumentation can cause perforation or cervical injury.

symptoms: Vaginal bleeding in early pregnancy, with or without passage of tissue
Fever, chills, foul-smelling discharge after an abortion (CAC 2023 p. 51)
Dizziness or fainting from blood loss
physicalSigns: Open cervical os with tissue at the os (incomplete)
Pallor, fast weak pulse 110/min or more, systolic under 90 mmHg (CAC 2023 p. 50)
Rebound tenderness, distended abdomen (infection or perforation) (CAC 2023 p. 51)
redFlags: Shock: pulse 110/min or more, systolic under 90 mmHg, respiration 30/min or more, confusion (CAC 2023 p. 50)
Heavy bright red bleeding soaking pads (CAC 2023 p. 49)
Fever with foul discharge and abdominal pain: septic abortion (NTG section 6.3)
Severe pain, rigidity or shoulder pain after a procedure: perforation (CAC 2023 p. 49)
Persistent pain unrelieved by analgesia: exclude ectopic pregnancy (CAC 2023 p. 60)
precipitants: Retained products after medical or surgical abortion

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Empty uterus with adnexal mass or free fluid; cervical motion tenderness (CAC 2023 p. 30).
Uterus larger than dates, soft (CAC 2023 p. 31); very high hCG; snowstorm appearance on ultrasound.
Closed os, live intrauterine pregnancy on ultrasound (NICE 1.5).
Erosion or growth that bleeds on touch on speculum examination (CAC 2023 p. 30).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Excessive or prolonged bleeding, pallor, pain or fever with retained products of conception.
Fever, vaginal discharge and pelvic or abdominal pain after abortion; with organ dysfunction, peritonitis or severe pain = sepsis.
No heartbeat with crown–rump length 7 mm or more, or mean sac diameter 25 mm or more with no fetal pole, confirmed by second opinion or repeat scan after 7 days.

ruleIn.normalValue: Intrauterine pregnancy with heartbeat, or empty uterus after complete miscarriage
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Retained products, no heartbeat, or no intrauterine sac
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Confirms type of miscarriage; excludes ectopic; not mandatory where unavailable (CAC 2023 pp. 31, 57).

clinicalManagement.title: Stabilise
actions: Shock: open airway, oxygen 6–8 L/min, Ringer lactate 1 litre in 15–20 minutes through a 16–18 gauge cannula, keep warm, intravenous antibiotics, transfuse if needed (CAC 2023 p. 50).
Evacuate retained products if suspected once resuscitation starts (CAC 2023 p. 50).

clinicalManagement.title: Control bleeding
actions: Misoprostol and uterine massage for uterine bleeding (CAC 2023 p. 49).
Continuing bleeding: oxytocin 10 units in 500 mL Ringer lactate or normal saline at 40–60 drops/min (CAC 2023 p. 49).
Cervical tear: pressure, then absorbable suture (CAC 2023 p. 49).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat retained products
actions: Incomplete abortion: misoprostol or vacuum aspiration up to 12 weeks under antibiotic cover (CAC 2023 pp. 38, 51).
Missed miscarriage: expectant for 7–14 days, or mifepristone then misoprostol, or vacuum aspiration (NICE 1.5.4, 1.5.11).

clinicalManagement.title: Septic abortion
actions: Blood and cervical cultures, then intravenous antibiotics (NTG section 6.3).
Evacuate retained products; it is crucial for response (NTG section 6.3). Take care: an infected uterus perforates more easily (CAC 2023 p. 51).

clinicalManagement.title: Before discharge
actions: Anti-D for Rh-negative women; iron-folic acid for 3 months; contraception counselling (CAC 2023 p. 47).

branches.label: Incomplete abortion
branches.entryCriteria: Bleeding with retained products under 12 weeks, haemodynamically stable (CAC 2023 p. 51).

branches.label: Missed miscarriage
branches.entryCriteria: Non-viable intrauterine pregnancy with sac still in the uterus, woman chooses medical management (NICE 1.5.11).

branches.label: Threatened miscarriage
branches.entryCriteria: Bleeding with a scan-confirmed intrauterine pregnancy and a previous miscarriage (NICE 1.5.2).

branches.label: Post-abortion haemorrhage
branches.entryCriteria: Continued bleeding from the uterine cavity after misoprostol and massage (CAC 2023 p. 49).

branches.label: Septic abortion without organ dysfunction
branches.entryCriteria: Fever, discharge, pelvic pain after abortion, no organ dysfunction (NTG section 6.3).

branches.label: Septic abortion with organ dysfunction
branches.entryCriteria: Peritonitis, severe pain, bleeding or organ dysfunction (NTG section 6.3).

branches.label: Supportive care
branches.entryCriteria: All women after miscarriage or abortion procedures (CAC 2023 p. 47).

medicationPlan.note: Indian sources first: misoprostol, oxytocin, anti-D and ibuprofen from MoHFW CAC 2023; septic abortion antibiotics from NCDC-ICMR NTG 2025 section 6.3. Missed and threatened miscarriage regimens from NICE NG126 because the CAC guideline does not cover them. Evacuation of retained products is the key to source control. Not clinically reviewed.

teaching.scope: Early pregnancy loss and abortion complications.
learningObjectives: Treat septic abortion with antibiotics and evacuation.
keyPoints: Shock after abortion: fluids, antibiotics, evacuate.
Incomplete abortion: misoprostol 400 micrograms sublingual or vacuum aspiration.
Septic abortion: cultures, antibiotics within the hour, remove retained products.
Anti-D for Rh-negative women after evacuation.
pitfalls: Missing an ectopic pregnancy in a woman with pain after medical abortion.
Treating septic abortion with antibiotics alone without evacuating the uterus.
Rough evacuation of an infected uterus (perforation risk).
Forgetting contraception and iron after the episode.

patientEducation: Some bleeding and cramps are normal; heavy bleeding, fever, severe pain or vomiting need urgent review (CAC 2023 p. 47).
A period usually returns in 3–6 weeks; pregnancy can occur before then (CAC 2023 p. 47).
Miscarriage is common and usually not caused by anything the woman did.
lifestyleAndDiet: Normal diet the same day; restrict activity for 3 days; avoid douching; avoid intercourse for a week or until bleeding stops (CAC 2023 p. 47).
Iron-folic acid tablets for at least 3 months (CAC 2023 p. 47).
mdtReferrals: Higher centre with blood transfusion for haemoglobin under 7 g/dL, perforation or sepsis (CAC 2023 pp. 32, 49)
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review in 1–2 weeks (CAC 2023 p. 47); urine pregnancy test at 3 weeks after medical management of miscarriage (NICE 1.5).
